name: Inclisiran
drug_class: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) PCSK9 synthesis inhibitor
route_note: subcutaneous injection by a healthcare professional at day 0, month 3, then every 6 months

discovery.note: Licensed to The Medicines Company in 2013, which Novartis acquired in 2020.

tagline: Twice-yearly siRNA that silences PCSK9 production in the liver
summary: Inclisiran is a GalNAc-conjugated small interfering RNA that switches off production of PCSK9 in liver cells. Given by injection twice a year after initial doses, it lowers LDL cholesterol by about 50%.
mechanism: The siRNA is conjugated to N-acetylgalactosamine, which binds the asialoglycoprotein receptor and delivers it selectively into hepatocytes.

Inside the cell its antisense strand is loaded into the RNA-induced silencing complex, which cleaves PCSK9 messenger RNA. Less PCSK9 protein is made, so more LDL receptors recycle to the cell surface and LDL clearance increases.
Because the loaded silencing complex persists for months, the effect lasts long after the drug has left the plasma.
uses: Primary hypercholesterolaemia (including heterozygous FH) or mixed dyslipidaemia, as an adjunct to diet with or without statins

history.title: Licensing
history.detail: Alnylam licenses the PCSK9 siRNA programme to The Medicines Company.

history.title: ORION-10 and -11
history.detail: Phase 3 trials show about 50% LDL reduction with twice-yearly dosing.

history.title: Novartis acquisition and EU approval
history.detail: Novartis completes its acquisition of The Medicines Company; the EU approves Leqvio in December.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US in December, after an earlier delay related to manufacturing inspection.

history.title: Label broadened
history.detail: The US label is updated to allow earlier use in primary hyperlipidaemia.

pk.half_life: ~9 h in plasma (pharmacodynamic effect lasts months)
pk.bioavailability: Subcutaneous; rapidly taken up by the liver

facts: It was the first siRNA approved for a common disease rather than a rare one.
Cardiovascular outcome trials (ORION-4, VICTORION-2 PREVENT) were ongoing at the time of writing.

references.title: Ray KK et al. Two phase 3 trials of inclisiran in patients with elevated LDL cholesterol (ORION-10/11). N Engl J Med 2020
